newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Fidelity Investments positive on Nordic companies.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Investments positive on Nordic companies.

text.p: International fund management company Fidelity Investments said on Wednesday it saw scope for growth among Nordic companies.
"Our analysts are more positive about the management and growth for Nordic companies than for central European ones," Colin Stone, a Fidelity investment director, told a news conference.
He spoke in connection with the opening of Fidelity's Stockholm branch office.
"Industry by industry, Nordic companies are undervalued in relation to their European peers," he said. "Dollar by dollar you can buy a better quality of business in the Nordic region."

The current pick-up in the economy will benefit some Swedish small companies, such as telecoms and certain IT companies, while industrial companies are likely to be hurt by the stronger Swedish crown.
"Swedish (industrial) small caps are experiencing a margin squeeze following the strengthening of the crown in the past 18 months," he said.
"We see this margin pressure unwind in the next 12 months, but we are likely to see earnings disappointment in (industrial) Swedish small caps in the next six to 12 months."
In general, Stone said Fidelity was more biased toward small companies. "You are not overpaying for European small companies at the moment," he said.
